subject: UCM v0.1 r032 native completion review transport

identity_observed.predecessor: r031: qualification bdb2b458..., identity ea3511bb..., source 603b6e4d... all equal my r031 observations in full

verdict_basis: Two MED findings. R32-01: the C17 native core refuses profile-valid programs the Python reference accepts (work-order item 5). R32-02: acceptance closure test R32-05 fails a clean replay on both supported interpreters because it is not hermetic (work-order item 3). Everything else holds: custody exact; release, cold boot and operator kit rebuild byte-identical on 3.12.3 and 3.13.16; the five-program corpus corresponds exactly on a third platform under gcc and clang; R31-01 and R31-02 closed; R31-03 repaired with a narrow residual.

findings.title: The C17 core cannot read the register sets the declared profile allows
evidence: native/ucm_native_core.c reads every line with fgets into MAX_LINE=512 bytes. The REGISTERS header carries all register values on one line; the profile and validate_native_program allow 256 i64 registers (a line of up to 5,390 bytes).

Positive exercise with profile-valid programs built by build_native_program: Python reference PASS in every case; the C core (gcc and clang, -std=c17 -Werror) PASS only while the REGISTERS line is at most 511 bytes. Full-width values: 23 registers PASS, 24 refuse (NATIVE_PROGRAM_HEADER_INVALID), 100/255/256 refuse (NATIVE_REGISTER_COUNT_MISMATCH). Zero values: 100 PASS, 255 and 256 refuse.
The five corpus programs never approach a declared limit, so the witnesses and court cannot see this.
findings.contradicts: Work order item 5 ('C17 ... and Python reference realization agree exactly'); docs/UCM-NATIVE-COMPLETION.md ('it is not allowed to silently widen the C profile'); profile limits.max_registers 256.
findings.impact: Fail-closed: the C core refuses with a typed code and never returns a wrong value. But the native execution authority covers only part of its own declared profile, and the declared 256-register limit is unreachable.
findings.repair: Size the line buffer to the profile maximum (or emit one register per line), and add boundary programs to the frozen corpus: 256 registers at I64_MIN/I64_MAX, 4096 instructions, the 1,000,000-step bound and the 1024 stack bound.

findings.title: Acceptance closure test R32-05 depends on an importable ucm outside the qualified source
evidence: test_native_core_r032.test_cli_and_abi_expose_portable_fallback runs [sys.executable, '-m', 'ucm.cli', ...] with cwd=ROOT and no PYTHONPATH. Other CLI tests (e.g. test_public_surface) set PYTHONPATH=ROOT/src.
Clean replay from an empty environment fails it on both 3.12.3 and 3.13.16: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ucm'. Rerun with PYTHONPATH=src it passes on both.
The receipt records PASS on the builder's 3.12.10, so ucm was importable there from outside the qualification's own path setup, possibly an installed copy rather than the qualified source.
This test is the direct closure check for acceptance case R32-05.
findings.impact: The replay leg fails on clean supported hosts (463/466 rather than the expected 464/466), and the R32-05 closure on the builder may have exercised a different ucm than the bytes qualified.
findings.repair: Pass env PYTHONPATH=ROOT/src (or invoke tools/ucm.py) in the test, and have qualification refuse when an installed ucm shadows the source.

findings.title: R31-03 residual: the external pin binds the header's root label, not the rows
findings.evidence: ucm_archive_verify.c compares argv[3] with the header's manifest_root string, and the trailer's row digest is declared by the same manifest. By source, a truncated manifest with its header count and trailer recomputed passes. Damage and naive truncation now refuse, as the doc says.
findings.repair: Pin the row-stream digest externally (emit it beside the manifest root in a Python receipt and pass it as a fourth argument), or document that only accidental truncation is in scope.

findings.title: Observations
items: The C core accepts non-canonical integer spellings (strtoimax allows leading whitespace and '+') and ignores bytes after the END line (program_sha256 still covers them). Its digests are self-declared, so it executes any self-consistent projection within the profile; no external program_root is pinned.

The r031 programs and courts are not yet frozen: both registries are unchanged at 28 program and 18 operator rows. review/r031 has no PROVENANCE.json, unlike r028/r029; r032 binds it through its source denominator instead.
The r031 work selections keep their 'tests.' ids (historical, unchanged); with R28-07 and R20-01 they do not resolve against the current receipt.
The fallback test's child interpreter runs without -B and writes bytecode into the source tree during qualification.
R21-01 secondary items; sim.add parameter shape checked only at evaluation.
r015-r017, r025 and r030 never reviewed; two Windows-only tests; wheel test needs setuptools; receipt root depends on Python patch version; case probe writes transiently.
